column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/helm-auto-release.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran
# cargo-auto-release. The run reported SUCCESS: `bump` bumped, tagged and
# pushed; `ship` was SKIPPED; the crate was never published; nothing said so.
# The condition was `needs.bump.outputs.bumped == 'true' && !github.event.
# repository.private`, which is correct and deliberate — publishing from a
# private repo leaks code to crates.io and undoes yanks. The failure was that
# nobody had written down which jobs must run for a given input, so a
# deliberate no-publish and a broken no-publish were the same green tick.
# WHAT THE SWEEP FOUND HERE, and the reason to read this header before editing
# a row. helm-auto-release does NOT share that shape. Both of its
# `github.event.repository.private` occurrences are in `runs-on:` — runner
# routing only (private caller -> the camelot-builder-pleme-eks ARC pool,
# public caller -> ubuntu-latest). NEITHER is in an `if:`. So `ship` packages
# and pushes the chart to the OCI registry from a PRIVATE caller exactly as it
# does from a public one. Whether that is the intended posture for charts is a
# decision this table does not make; it records the behaviour so the decision
# is visible instead of implicit.
# Rows 1 and 2 therefore differ ONLY in a context key that no condition reads,
# and that is deliberate — it is the tripwire. The day someone copies
# cargo-auto-release's `&& !github.event.repository.private` onto `ship`, row 2
# turns NOT-RUN and the change lands as a decision rather than as a silent stop
# to every private chart's publishing.
# TABLE RULES that make these rows verbose on purpose:
#   - every context path any condition touches must be declared in EVERY case;
#     an undeclared path is an ERROR, not an empty default, so an incomplete
#     case can never become a confident verdict;
#   - an EMPTY value (needs.bump.outputs.bumped=) models a SKIPPED upstream
#     job, which is a distinct state from 'false';
#   - `ship` needs `bump` and does not call always(), so a skipped `bump`
#     propagates to a skipped `ship` — rows 4 and 5 pin that.
# NOT ASSERTED, because it is outside what job selection can see: this table
# proves `ship` is SELECTED, never that the chart became resolvable. That is
# the job's own final step ("verify the published chart is resolvable"), which
# runs inside `ship` and is a different layer of check.
# 1. The healthy public release. Both jobs run; nothing is skipped.
public-bump
# 2. A PRIVATE caller that bumped still publishes — unlike cargo-auto-release,
# this workflow has no privacy guard on `ship`. Asserted, not assumed.
private-bump-still-publishes
# 3. Nothing under source-paths changed, so helm-bump reports bumped=false and
# `ship` must skip. A no-op run is a legitimate green, and this row is what
# distinguishes it from a broken one.
public-no-bump
# 4. Same no-bump outcome from a private caller: the skip is driven by the bump
# result, never by visibility. Pairs with row 2 to pin that visibility changes
# NOTHING about which jobs select in this workflow.
private-no-bump
# 5. The loop guard. `bump` pushes a commit as the bot, and that push re-enters
# this workflow; `if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'` stops the second
# pass. `bump` is skipped, so `bumped` is EMPTY (not 'false'), and `ship` is
# skipped by needs-propagation — it never calls always(). If `ship` ever grows
# an always(), this row goes RAN and the re-publish loop is caught here.
bot-actor-no-loop
